history.period: First mentioned before 784 CE; present structure 15th century
history.summary: IDENTITY NOTE - sources disagree on this shrine's sectarian identity. Wikipedia's 'Ambika Temple, Girnar' identifies it as a temple to the JAIN goddess Ambika (a yakshi), first mentioned in the 8th century with the present structure built in the 15th century. Most travel sources describe the same hilltop shrine as the HINDU Amba Mata Temple - a Shakti shrine with no idol, only a golden yantra inscribed with 51 shlokas, plus footprints of the goddess and her chariot; it is famously visited by newlywed couples for marital blessings. The two descriptions may refer to the same structure venerated by both traditions (verify). Inscriptions record minister Vastupala's pilgrimage in Vikram Samvat 1249 (1192 CE); Vastupala and Tejapala built its mandapa and parikara, and merchant Shamla restored it in VS 1524 (1468 CE). The temple sits near a Girnar summit (~600 m height); step counts in sources vary from 2,000 to 5,000 from the base - CONFLICT (verify). The 2020 Girnar ropeway (2,320 m) reaches close to the temple. Coordinates taken from Wikipedia; the geocoder could not resolve the summit precisely - approximate (verify on ground).

name: Amba Mata Temple, Girnar
town_description: Junagadh is a historic city at the foot of Girnar hill in the Saurashtra region of Gujarat. It was the capital of the Chudasama Rajputs and later the Babi Nawabs, and holds Uparkot Fort, Ashoka's rock edicts, and the Mahabat Maqbara. The city is the gateway to the Girnar pilgrimage - sacred to Jains, Hindus, and Muslims alike - with Bhavnath Taleti at the hill's base.

travel.railway: Junagadh railway station (~6 km from Bhavnath Taleti) (verify)
travel.road: Girnar ropeway from Bhavnath Taleti reaches within ~50 steps of the temple (verify); otherwise a long climb up the hill steps
